traversal_review.input: Review this crawler traversal issue using only these observations. Public print-product form initially has only Shape. After selecting Rectangle it has Size choices, but Orientation becomes visible only after the first size is selected. Horizontal and Vertical use disjoint size IDs. A DFS selects all currently visible controls; it prioritizes Orientation when present, but it locks Size into its prefix before Orientation first appears. Saved data covers one Rectangle size although later snapshots advertise 22 size choices. Explain the likely missed-domain mechanism and a safe bounded correction plus a regression test, in at most 180 words. Do not invent prices, claim live verification, or suggest narrowing the requested catalog.
traversal_review.model_response:
The form is conditionally dependent: Orientation is hidden until Size selected, and Size IDs differ by orientation. DFS that enumerates currently visible controls will pick a Size to reveal Orientation, then fix that Size in the path prefix while branching on Orientation. That locks exploration to sizes compatible with the first-picked Size's orientation family, missing the other family's IDs. Later snapshots showing 22 sizes reflect UI after both orientations explored, but saved records only contain the first branch, hence one Rectangle size.

Correction: make traversal orientation-aware with bounded backtracking: when new control appears, re-expand predecessor choices that gate it, limited to e.g. Rectangle x Sizes x Orientations, with visited-state dedup on (shape,size-id,orientation). Do not unboundedly crawl.

Regression: seed Rectangle, select first size, assert Orientation appears, then assert crawler revisits Size list under both Horizontal and Vertical and saves >1 distinct size-id, and that count matches snapshot's advertised size options.
traversal_review.status: advisory; implementation and browser regression verified separately
